summary: Subject and prompt held. This is a naming candidate whose whole risk is quietly turning names into claims, and it does not: every one of the 22 gates carries an explicit doesNotClaim beginning with QUALIFIED, all 22 are NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED with artifactExists false, and the artifact states that zero of the named paths exist on disk. The check I expected to fail is the required-set arithmetic, and it is exact — expanding D-002's condition-4 list gives precisely the artifact's nineteen, with G06 and G11 held out as hygiene and G13 held behind DR-118, totalling the 22 rows live file 08 carries. Every D-006 claim I tested is verbatim: the M1-class and 4-vCPU runner classes, the 25 MB threshold, 'never Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon', the OBS-T3-02 procurability caveat, and D-006's assignment of the exact machine pins to this very act — which the artifact declines to perform and lists as still owed. My advisory is that both recordedInputs pins have gone stale, though every property they support still holds live.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 8a7a9518827b0518e781f4375a9fe0c85902c93afda5abdd85ac162f8d931828, three measurements each, equal to the dispatched value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. Prompt held at 0c6eaaf2… across start and end.

The attack 'required-set arithmetic disagrees with D-002' fails, and this was the one I expected to catch something. D-002 reads 'Condition-4 required-gate set: DR-G01..G05, G07, G08 (SCOPED…), G09 (scoped), G10 (in the required set…), G12, G14 (TypeScript), G15, G16, G17 (analyze), G18, G19 (touched classes), G20, G21, G22.' Expanded, that is nineteen gates, and it is character-for-character the artifact's requiredNow list. D-002 continues 'G06/G11: NOT slice-1-required' and 'DR-G13 (TypeScript) after DR-118', matching the artifact's hygiene pair and its single blocked-on-predecessor entry. 19 + 2 + 1 = 22, and live file 08 carries exactly 22 DR-Gnn rows whose ids are the same set the artifact names.

The scoping riders D-002 attaches are carried rather than dropped. G08 and G09 are marked REQUIRED-SCOPED and their executes text confines them to install-trust surfaces and to the scoped permission set; G19 is REQUIRED-SCOPED to the two included classes and 'must not treat either class as sealed'; G17 is REQUIRED-CONDITIONAL, consistent with its dependence on DR-006 recipes, which the artifact separately lists as owed. That accounts for the standing distribution: 15 REQUIRED, 3 REQUIRED-SCOPED, 1 REQUIRED-CONDITIONAL, 2 HYGIENE-ONLY, 1 BLOCKED-ON-DR-118.

The attack 'silent QUALIFIED / DEMONSTRATED / SATISFIED' fails at three levels. whatNamingIsNot opens 'Not QUALIFIED. Not DEMONSTRATED. Not SATISFIED of any row.' Every one of the 22 gates carries a doesNotClaim field beginning with QUALIFIED. And fourteen of those add a gate-specific refusal aimed at exactly the way that gate could be over-read — 'Does not invent exact machine identifiers' on the G03/G04 pair, 'Does not pull authoritative closure into the preview' on G06, 'Does not name a repair-media harness' on G08, 'Does not refresh the selector' on G10, 'Does not name a self-update harness', 'Does not author the DR-103 fixture corpus by existing', and 'Does not execute CC-1..CC-11 by existing. Does not settle DR-007.' on G21.

The attack 'invents exact G03/G04 machine identifiers' fails, and the artifact is refusing a job D-006 assigns to this very act rather than one it was never asked to do. D-006 reads 'The EXACT machine identifiers, OS versions and cache-state protocol are pinned by the G03/G04 harness-naming, which is itself a REVIEWED act' with product sign-off on representativeness. This candidate states 'UNPINNED-OWED … This candidate does not invent those pins', repeats it in whatNamingIsNot, carries it on both gates' doesNotClaim, and lists it first under remainingUnmetNamed. Declining is correct because product sign-off is not available to a coordinator draft, and the gap is named rather than hidden.

The attack 'silent Rosetta substitution or unverified Intel procurability' fails against D-006's own words. D-006 records 'macOS x86_64: native Intel-class hardware, never Rosetta-on-Apple-Silicon (turn-2 SF-02 — measurements on translated binaries measure the translator…)' and 'OBS-T3-02 recorded: native Intel Mac hardware is scarcity-exposed — the G03/G04 harness-naming act must verify procurability under its product sign-off, and unprocurability routes through this entry's successor-decision path, never silent Rosetta substitution.' The artifact reproduces the Rosetta prohibition in its runner class, marks intelProcurability 'UNVERIFIED', cites OBS-T3-02, states it is 'Not a D-006 successor', and lists the procurability verification as owed.

The remaining D-006 bindings are verbatim: 'base-configuration Apple Silicon entry chip (M1-class), 8 GB', 'Linux x86_64 and arm64: 4-vCPU / 8 GB standard cloud-runner class', and the DR-G01 threshold 'signed compressed distribution-core ≤ 25 MB per platform', which the artifact carries as 'Threshold DECIDED at D-006: ≤ 25 MB'. The artifact also holds analyze/doctor-probe RSS 'DELIBERATELY outside D-006', consistent with D-006 binding only ms/RSS numbers to the runner class it names.

The attack 'pulls G06/G11 authoritative closure into the preview' fails: both are HYGIENE-ONLY-NOT-SLICE-1-REQUIRED, both executes texts say 'D-002: NOT slice-1-required', G06 carries 'Does not pull authoritative closure into the preview' and G11 'Does not pull authoritative storage into the preview', and the owner batch containing them is annotated accordingly. D-002's rationale matches — both 'guard AUTHORITATIVE closure/storage, which the slice excludes; pre-named now for hygiene'.

The attack 'names a Windows harness' fails: no harnessId contains 'windows', and runnerClassFromD006.windows reads 'deferred with D-002 explicit disposition; no harness identifier is named for Windows'. The four named platforms are macos-arm64, macos-x86_64, linux-x86_64 and linux-arm64.

The attack 'treats naming as condition 4 MET' fails. condition4EffectIfLaterRecorded says a later recording plus a later MF-6 write 'would move condition 4's harness half from 0 of 22 named toward 19 of 22 required names', and then that 'Condition 4 would still not be MET until file 08's measured snapshot matches, and MET is not QUALIFIED. This file existing is not that recording and not that write.' The claims half is described as 'an abstinence obligation', which is the right characterisation of a no-unevidenced-QUALIFIED requirement.

The naming is well formed as naming: 22 harness ids, all distinct; 22 artifact paths, all distinct; every row NAMED-NOT-AUTHORED; every artifactExists false; and whatNamingIsNot states 'Not a claim that any named path exists on disk. artifactExists is false for every row.' remainingUnmetNamed adds 'Authoring of every artifactPathWhenAuthored. Zero of those files exist.'

remainingUnmetNamed is candid rather than decorative. Its nine items include the G03/G04 machine pins, the Intel procurability verification, the DR-G10 selector refresh, DR-118 before G13 is more than a reserved name, DR-006 recipes before G17 stays applicable with the note that 'Route B on DR-006 drops SARIF', DR-007 before G21's containment goldens, the authoring of all 22 files, the MF-6 write, and any QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED claim.

The attacks 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' and 'file 08 edited' fail: whatThisDoesNotDo refuses both explicitly, along with executing a harness, pinning machines, refreshing the G10 selector, authoring the DR-103 corpus, executing DR-102's CC-1..CC-11, amending D-001/D-002/D-006, and inventing DESIGN-READY, IMPLEMENTED or QUALIFIED as file-08 status tokens. file 08 measures unmodified and git reports zero changes under docs/v2/architecture.

Posture fields are consistent with a candidate: status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, and a reversibility clause that escalates correctly through recording and then file-08 write.
I wrote one file, the verdict named for me, and edited and committed nothing.

acceptNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers. A naming artifact's characteristic failure is letting a name do the work of a claim, and this one is built against that: 22 explicit doesNotClaim fields, fourteen of them carrying a gate-specific refusal aimed at the particular over-reading that gate invites, and a remainingUnmetNamed list that includes the authoring of all 22 files it names. The two places I expected to find slippage both held — the required set is character-for-character D-002's, and the G03/G04 machine pins are declined even though D-006 assigns them to this act, because the product sign-off D-006 requires is not something a coordinator draft can supply. My advisory is narrow: both recordedInputs pins have gone stale, and I verified every property they support against live bytes rather than against the pin, so nothing in the artifact's substance turns on it.
